faqs.question: What happens in the free consultation?
faqs.answer: We spend up to 30 minutes understanding your business, your goals and the features you need. You can ask about websites, logos, hosting, email, IT support or phone systems. We then confirm a suitable scope and quote. Submitting a request starts a conversation; it does not book a calendar slot or commit you to a purchase.

faqs.question: Can you design my logo as well as my website?
faqs.answer: Yes. Custom logo packs start at $110 AUD and include common logo dimensions for your online presence, plus up to 30 minutes of consulting to understand your vision. Website design and implementation packages start at $50, $150 and $500 AUD. We agree on deliverables during consultation.

faqs.question: Where will my website be hosted?
faqs.answer: We offer hosting in Melbourne and Sydney data centres, with US and UK options for international customers. We work with people around the world and help select a location close to your audience for lower latency. Availability is confirmed when we prepare your quote.

faqs.question: What is included in the hosting platform?
faqs.answer: Our Virtualmin Pro platform uses a LEMP stack: Linux, Nginx, MariaDB/MySQL and PHP. It supports domain and DNS management, databases, SSL certificate management, SFTP access and backup scheduling. Access, retention and individual features depend on your plan and configuration, which we confirm during consultation. Each standard hosting plan includes SSL and deployment of the stated page count, or a choice of 60+ one-click applications.

faqs.question: Do hosted email plans have lock-in contracts?
faqs.answer: No. Both hosted IMAP email options have no lock-in contracts. Basic Email is $6 AUD per seat per month on our shared platform with 10 GB cloud storage. Pro Email is $60 AUD per five seats per month on a private virtual server with 60 GB cloud storage. Both include CalDAV calendars, spam filtering and antivirus. We confirm storage allocation and migration needs in your quote.

faqs.question: Can you help with our network or business phones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Server and infrastructure support, including MikroTik networking, starts at $150 AUD per hour. PC, desktop and laptop support is $110 AUD per hour. We also offer hosted 3CX and FreePBX phone systems, quoted after discussing your users and the features you need.

posts.title: How to choose web hosting for a small business
posts.excerpt: Storage, bandwidth, location and support: what actually matters when you pick a hosting plan, and what you can safely ignore.
posts.author: WebTechPros team
posts.body:
Hosting plans are full of numbers, but only a few of them matter for most small business websites. Here's how to read a plan without getting lost.

1. Location matters more than you think

The closer your server is to your visitors, the faster your pages load. If most of your customers are in Australia, Australian hosting is the simple choice. We host in Melbourne and Sydney, with US and UK options.

2. Storage and bandwidth: buy for the next year, not the next decade

A typical brochure website uses well under 1 GB of storage. Online stores and sites with lots of images or downloads need more. Start with a plan that fits today and leaves room to grow; you can move up later.

  • Up to 5 GB: most small business and portfolio sites
  • Up to 10 GB: growing sites, blogs with lots of images
  • Up to 30 GB: larger sites and online stores

3. SSL should be included

Browsers warn visitors about sites without HTTPS. An SSL certificate should come with the plan, not as an extra.

4. Ask who you'll talk to when something breaks

The cheapest plans often come with ticket queues and scripted answers. Check whether you can reach a real person who can look at your actual site.

The best hosting plan is the one you never have to think about.

Compare our hosting plans, or book a free consultation and we'll recommend one.

posts.title: Five signs your website needs a refresh
posts.excerpt: If your site is hard to use on a phone or you're embarrassed to share the link, it's probably time.
posts.author: WebTechPros team
posts.body:
Websites age faster than most businesses do. Here are five signs yours is due for an update.

1. It's hard to use on a phone

Most visitors arrive on mobile. If they have to pinch and zoom, they'll leave.

2. Customers can't find the basics

Opening hours, prices, a phone number and how to book should be one tap away.

3. It's slow

Every extra second of loading costs visitors. Modern hosting and lighter pages help.

4. You can't update it yourself

If changing a price means emailing a developer, your site will always be out of date.

5. You're embarrassed to share the link

Your website is often the first impression. It should make you proud.
